newsitem.title: UK: Clarke tops first UK Conservative leadership vote.
newsitem.headline: Clarke tops first UK Conservative leadership vote.

text.p: Former finance minister Kenneth Clarke came top of the first ballot held on Tuesday to succeed John Major as leader of Britain's main opposition Conservative party but failed to get enough votes to win outright.
Sir Archie Hamilton, chairman of the 1922 committee of Conservative backbenchers, which organised the ballot, said the party's 164 members of parliament voted for the five candidates as follows:
Clarke would have needed 83 votes plus a margin of 15 percent over his nearest challenger to have won on the first ballot.
A second round of voting will now take place next Tuesday,
Any Conservative MP can stand in the second ballot, including those who did not contest the first round.
Nominations must be submitted by 1100 GMT on June 12.
To win on the second ballot, a simple majority(83 votes)is needed.
If there is no winner on June 17, the two front-runners will square off in a third and final ballot on June 19.
